welcome.text: Morning, {called}. On time. I'm almost disappointed.
Welcome to the skills lab. Six stations. Everything you break in here is plastic.
Scrubbing, monitors, histories, instruments, IV lines, stitches. You'll use every one of them in theatre, usually all at once.
Pick a station. Mistakes are free today. Tomorrow they're not.
welcome.head: nod

scrub_intro.text: Theatre rule one: nothing dirty touches the patient. That includes you.
Water. Soap. Every part of both hands, properly. Rinse, towel, gown, gloves. In that order.
And once you've soaped, don't touch your face. Not your mask, not your nose. I'm watching.
scrub_intro.head: nod

monitor_intro.text: This screen talks to you all operation long. Most people stop listening. Then it starts screaming.
Learn the four numbers. Then I'll show you patients, and you tell me what's wrong before it's too late.
monitor_intro.head: nod

history_intro.text: Half of surgery is asking the right question before the knife comes out.
I'll be the patient. Mr. Kumar. You get five questions. Find what could hurt him on the table.

instruments_intro.text: Tom D'Souza. Scrub nurse. I hand you things, you don't drop them. That's our whole relationship.
First, match each job to the right instrument. Then Dr. Iyer calls for things and you tell me, fast.

iv_intro.text: An IV line. You'll do a hundred of these before you do one operation.
Choose a good vein, get the angle right, and keep your hand still. The arm is plastic. Pretend it isn't.
iv_intro.head: nod

stitch_intro.text: Every operation ends the same way: someone has to close.
Stitches across the cut, end to end, evenly spaced. Patients judge you by the scar, not the surgery.

again.text: Again? Good. Habits are built, not born.

done.text: Six for six. I've seen worse. I've also seen better, but I'm in a good mood.
Tomorrow you assist me in theatre. Appendectomy. A student called Rohit, nineteen. Read his notes tonight.

then.text: Everyone's ready until the first cut. We'll see.
then.head: nod

then.text: Good. Nervous people wash their hands properly.
He's busy. He has a very full stomach.
